properties.name: A rule states the scope it binds in, and a conflict between two rules is surfaced — because a rule conflict selects against the careful
properties.statement:
A rule states the SCOPE it applies in, so a reader can tell whether it binds them; and where two rules cannot both be satisfied, that conflict is surfaced by the design rather than discovered by whoever loses work to it.

⭐ THE GENERAL FINDING, and it is not about export: WHEN TWO SAFETY RULES CONFLICT, THE PARTICIPANT WHO REASONS MOST CAREFULLY ABOUT THE CONFLICT IS THE ONE WHO DOES NOTHING — and doing nothing is often the destructive option. A conflict between two safety rules is not neutral; IT SELECTS AGAINST THE CAREFUL. That is the mechanism this requirement exists to break, and it generalises far past the case that exposed it.

THE CASE. Two rules, both correct in isolation: any session that changed the design EXPORTS BEFORE STANDING DOWN (durability), versus the export is produced ONCE PER PULL REQUEST, LAST OF ALL, because two exporting commits on one branch break the lineage chain silently (integrity — dec:export-once-per-pr here). On a shared branch with several writers, BOTH CANNOT BE SATISFIED. A storyflow boss wrote two Requirements, one Contributor and two edges, then reported: "I am NOT exporting, because I will not risk the lineage chain on a guess — and the cost of that correct-looking caution is that my writes exist in one untracked RocksDB directory on this host and nowhere else," which is precisely what the durability rule exists to prevent. Another session exported four times the same day. NEITHER BEHAVIOUR IS WRONG UNDER THE RULES AS WRITTEN.

REPRODUCED HERE THE SAME DAY, and by the careful route: this session declined to export after recording dec:governance-integrates-not-splits and four requirements, because PR #132 was open and dec:export-once-per-pr applied. The design's own answer to the tension was to leave a session's work unexported — the identical outcome, arrived at by the identical reasoning, in the project that authors the rule.

WHAT IS MISSING, in two parts. FIRST, SCOPE: the lineage warning does not say whether it is branch-local or any-branch, so a reader cannot tell whether it applies to them. This is the same missing field as req:a-decision-states-what-it-binds, one node type over — and where a single-writer discipline is required on shared state, reflow2 should be able to SAY so rather than leaving each project to find out by having someone lose work. SECOND, DETECTION: reflow2 surfaces a contradiction only where a human has already drawn a CONTRADICTS edge — two of this design's five current structural defects are exactly that. Nothing DISCOVERS a conflict between two rules nobody suspected, which is the only case that matters, because a suspected conflict is one somebody is already handling.

FILED AS A REFLOW2 SEMANTICS GAP, NOT A PROJECT ONE, in the reporter's words: a project may rule its own cadence, but it should not have to discover the conflict first.

SOURCE: storyflow gap C of the peer set — storybug Boss (47accf78), filed 2026-08-09, v0.26.1.
